study.question: Can task-owned position-by-feedback-by-target-match routing exploit information absent from the incumbent permutation-invariant representation, and does preserving feedback identity matter specifically when feedback is bound to supplied event position?
study.hypothesis: Observation: source inspection of g3-r0013-local_collapsed shows the selector, values, additive evidence, static gate and local quadratic route are permutation equivariant over valid events before invariant pooling; no position enters. This is a structural limitation, not a measured order diagnostic. Local collapsed click AUC=0.6637100466058103, local resolved=0.6637033578973434; history-composition collapsed=0.6635657613671003 and resolved=0.6635072416589998. Thus the last factorial does not support history-summary conditioning or extra feedback identities in that route. The incumbent improves over g3-r0011-gate_redistribute_only=0.6633488027471348, but that is single-seed evidence for local capacity, not proof of mechanism. Hypothesis: the useful missing interaction is each event's feedback/match pattern with its valid-event distance from the supplied prefix end. Different task-owned kernels can change the selected evidence without allowing auxiliary gate parameters to rewrite click routing. Feedback identities that were redundant in position-free gates may become informative at different ranks. This is input-side feedback use; no claim that auxiliary supervision helps click. Prefix order is preserved by inspected upstream collator lines525-551 and579-598, but chronological generation and elapsed times are not established here; rank is explicitly positional.

nearest_work.difference: Exact local architectural parent, SHA256 e9514f0dba34c14d5587e9db5bc6a884b52bf81bda8012e442a792a0a9d7f9f5. Preserve every old path and append a task-specific position interaction. Unlike the failed history-summary replacement, position is attached to individual events.

Archived exact-version primary text lines250-283 inspected: target-conditioned unnormalized local activation, intensity rationale, and a reported unsuccessful LSTM attempt. Retain inherited local activation and measured click L1 redistribution. Add bounded scalar position-by-feedback routing; do not claim invention of attention, positional weighting, bilinear interactions or DIN reproduction.

Pinned benchmark primary implementation lines175-200 flattens the ordered item sequence with context before shared token mixing. Our route uses four event-rank kernels with task-owned 20x4 matrices on the existing history pooling; it does not adopt the full tokenizer, mixing stack or joint gradient topology. Original paper full text is unavailable in the authorized archive, so original-method novelty remains unverified.

Pinned benchmark source lines123-159 and278-313 inspected: feedback-specific sequence hubs, task tokens and learned broadcast. Here the new route reads input-only masks/matches and position, with no learned auxiliary donor, hub tokens or layer-wise broadcasts. This is a local difference from the inspected implementation, not a complete original-paper comparison.

Authorized primary benchmark section2.3 inspected, including UniMixer, task hubs and sequential transduction. These are alternatives for future matched studies; external reported effectiveness does not transfer automatically. No priority claim is made.

inherited_components: All code paths, embeddings, primary-owned selector trunk, auxiliary readout rows, private auxiliary item/action tables and task towers from g3-r0013-local_collapsed.
Input-only resolved additive feedback/match evidence; resolved event gate; collapsed local quadratic residual; live self donor and click coefficient-L1 redistribution; full auxiliary gains.
Shared user/context embeddings, field padding exclusions, task order from FeatureMap, frozen input visibility, data split, one-pass recipe, four unweighted BCEs, optimizers and host scoring.
Inherited initialization order and RNG stream. New torch.zeros parameter is allocated after the inherited reset and composition matrix; no additional reset or random sampling.
study.proposed_difference: For event i let e_i be its 20 exposure/feedback-by-target-match features, and r_i the count of valid supplied events strictly to its right. Define b_i,k=exp(-r_i/tau_k), tau=(1,4,16,64) valid-event counts. Add z_i,t=e_i^T P_t b_i / 2 to the inherited gate logit, P_t in R^(20x4), initialized to zero. Parent self-donor scales the entire click logit by1.5, then tanh bounds gains in(0,2); click coefficient L1 mass is restored exactly in FP32 except zero gated-mass fallback, then cast as inherited. Marginal replacement uses b_bar=(sum_valid b_i)/max(n,1) for every event; it retains history-length-dependent kernel means but removes event-position association. The identity factor averages only this NEW route's four feedback channels, preserving exposure and their sum (overlapping masks allowed). Parent evidence, linear gate and collapsed local route stay fixed in design across cells. All four task matrices and both event/marginal contractions are executed in each variant. No timestamp, current action, current label, global index, cross-example statistic, loss hook or filesystem/network operation is added. Position sensitivity and task ownership are candidate design, not established benefit.
predictions: Predeclared primary contrasts: click AUC(position_resolved)-click AUC(marginal_resolved)>0 and click AUC(position_collapsed)-click AUC(marginal_collapsed)>0 under the same frozen full-population validation recipe; report each difference, not only the winning cell. Click Logloss and all four task AUC/Logloss accompany selection.

Identity-by-position interaction: [AUC(position_resolved)-AUC(marginal_resolved)]-[AUC(position_collapsed)-AUC(marginal_collapsed)]>0 would provisionally support binding feedback type to position. A positive position main effect alone does not support that interaction or necessity of task-specific parameters.

On nonzero synthetic position weights, swapping two unequal-feedback/match events can change the event route and resulting pooling, whereas the marginal route remains permutation equivariant/invariant after pooling. At zero new weights every cell should match parent logits and raw inherited gradients before host clipping, subject to tensor verification. New parameter gradients differ across cells and can change the global dense clipping factor from the first update; inherited optimizer updates are not asserted identical.

Predeclared inherited history-length bins: empty (6444 samples/427 click positives),1-16 (461684/28818),17-64 (1001754/55298),>64 (1401885/50957). Negatives are samples minus positives. Longer histories offer more ranks, but no monotone slice improvement is assumed. Additional feedback-composition slices require pre-experiment definitions and host counts; not available locally.

New route contributes exactly zero on empty histories, gives equal event/marginal values on a single valid event, ignores arbitrary invalid-position payloads, and is invariant to adding padding while preserving valid-event order. Predictions for empty histories may still change after training through the shared optimizer and learned inherited parameters.
falsifiers: Neither ordered cell exceeding its own matched marginal control fails to support the proposed position-information benefit for this implementation. Improvement only against the old parent can be explained by added length-conditioned capacity.

A nonpositive identity-by-position contrast, or near-identical resolved/collapsed ordered results, fails to support the claimed feedback-specific position interaction. Do not rescue it by selecting an auxiliary mean AUC or a favorable exploratory slice.

Improvement restricted to auxiliary tasks does not meet the click selection objective. A click AUC gain with material Logloss/auxiliary degradation must be reported as a tradeoff, not universal positive transfer.

Failed masking, dependence on target action/current labels, nonfinite output/gradient, unintended cross-task gradient paths in the new route, or incompatible feature shapes invalidate the candidate before performance interpretation.

If a later budgeted paired-seed or paired user-cluster analysis does not retain the advantage, the one-seed result remains preliminary or unsupported. A null outcome does not refute every positional or sequence model.
alternative_explanations: Marginal controls retain only length-dependent positional summaries, not identical functional capacity. Parameter allocation and executed contractions match; effective feature ranks, optimization and gradient magnitudes differ. This is an information-removal replacement, not proof that all optimization confounds are eliminated.

Order could encode publisher sorting, truncation, exposure repetition or offline feedback maturation rather than recency of interest; no raw timestamps or point-in-time maturity audit is available. All conclusions are limited to the frozen official_offline benchmark.
Primary/auxiliary contexts and the host dense gradient-clip norm remain shared. Even task-owned matrices do not make task optimization independent; new auxiliary routes can affect click indirectly.

Prior g3-r0001-primary_feedback=0.6576086161503328 versus g3-r0001-joint_feedback=0.6554607825348479 and g3-r0003-embedding_item_primary=0.660163362657485 motivate ownership, but they predate private auxiliary tables and evidence gates; do not extrapolate magnitude.

Unsuccessful branches are retained: g3-r0006-learned_aux_transfer=0.659257496484386 and learned_self_transfer=0.658821147056956 did not beat g3-r0005-private_aux_items=0.6601638277860222; g3-r0012-redistrib_aux_detached=0.6630566462315345 trailed redistrib_self_live=0.6633488027471348. These limit donor-transfer claims, not all ways of using auxiliary labels.

Earlier g3-r0011-gate_redistribute_only=0.6633488027471348 exceeds full_control=0.6626801585674221, supporting the choice to hold mass normalization fixed. One seed and repeated selection over many successful-but-negative trajectories still permit selection noise. Byte-identical reruns are deterministic checks, not independent evidence.

Fixed event-count scales are a small prespecified basis and may miss relevant horizons; a negative run could reflect basis or single-pass optimization limitations. No local tuning on assessment data is allowed.
